The blessed person delights in God's law and meditates on it day and night. What would delighting in God's word look like for you?
The righteous is like a tree planted by streams of water. What keeps your roots watered?
"The Lord knows the way of the righteous." What comfort is there in being known by God?
The nations plot against the Lord and his Anointed. Where do you see people resisting God today?
God has set his King on Zion. How does this point to Jesus?
"Blessed are all who take refuge in him." What does it mean to take refuge in Jesus?
David's foes said, "There is no salvation for him in God." When have you felt surrounded?
"You, O Lord, are a shield about me, my glory, and the lifter of my head." Which of these do you need today?
David lay down and slept because the Lord sustained him. What helps you rest in God?
David asked God, "You have given me relief when I was in distress." How has God relieved you before?
"Be angry, and do not sin; ponder in your own hearts on your beds, and be silent." How do you handle anger?
"You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and wine abound." What joy does God give that things cannot?
"In the morning you hear my voice." How do you begin your day with God?
David asks God to lead him and make his way straight. Where do you need God's guidance?
"Let all who take refuge in you rejoice." What makes you glad in God?
David cried, "Be gracious to me, O Lord, for I am languishing." What makes you feel weak?
David was weary with moaning and flooded his bed with tears. How does God meet you in tears?
"The Lord has heard my plea." How does knowing God hears you change things?
David took refuge in God when pursued. Where do you run when you are attacked?
"God is a righteous judge." How does God's justice comfort you?
David gave thanks to the Lord for his righteousness. What can you thank God for?
"O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!" Where do you see God's majesty?
"What is man that you are mindful of him?" How does it feel that God is mindful of you?
God crowned people with glory and gave them care of creation. How can you care for God's world?
"I will give thanks to the Lord with my whole heart; I will recount all of your wonderful deeds." What deed of God would you recount?
"The Lord is a stronghold for the oppressed." Who needs God's stronghold?
"Those who know your name put their trust in you." How does knowing God help you trust him?
The psalmist asked, "Why, O Lord, do you stand far away?" When has God seemed far?
"You have seen... you note mischief and vexation." What does it mean that God sees injustice?
"You will strengthen their heart; you will incline your ear." How does God care for the afflicted?
"If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?" When have you felt shaken?
"The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord's throne is in heaven." How does this steady you?
The psalmist grieved that the godly were gone and lies spread. How do you respond to dishonesty around you?
"The words of the Lord are pure words, like silver refined." How do God's words differ from others'?
"How long, O Lord? Will you forget me forever?" When have you prayed "how long"?
David asked God to consider and answer him. What do you need God to answer?
"I have trusted in your steadfast love; my heart shall rejoice in your salvation." How did David's prayer turn?
"The fool says in his heart, 'There is no God.'" How do people live as if there is no God?
"There is none who does good, not even one." What does this show about our need for God?
David longed for salvation to come out of Zion. How does Jesus answer this longing?
"O Lord, who shall sojourn in your tent?" What would you answer?
David describes the one who walks blamelessly and speaks truth from the heart. Which quality do you want to grow in?
"I have no good apart from you." What does it mean that God is your greatest good?
"The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places." How has God's portion for you been good?
"In your presence there is fullness of joy." When have you known joy in God's presence?
David asked God to hear his just cause. What do you need God to hear?
"Keep me as the apple of your eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings." How does God protect you?
"When I awake, I shall be satisfied with your likeness." What satisfies you?
"I love you, O Lord, my strength. The Lord is my rock." Which name of God speaks to you?
God heard David's cry and rescued him. When has God drawn you out of deep waters?
"By my God I can leap over a wall." How does God strengthen you?
"The Lord lives, and blessed be my rock." How can you praise God today?
"The heavens declare the glory of God." What in creation shows you God's glory?
God's law revives the soul and rejoices the heart. How has God's word revived you?
"Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight." Pray this for your day.
"May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble." Who could you pray this over?
"Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the Lord." What do people trust in today?
The king rejoiced in God's strength and salvation. What victory has God given you?
"Be exalted, O Lord, in your strength! We will sing and praise your power." How can you praise his power?
"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" How does Jesus' use of this on the cross help you?
"Our fathers trusted, and you delivered them." How does God's faithfulness to others help your faith?
This psalm describes suffering that matches Jesus' crucifixion. What does this show about God's plan?
The psalm ends in praise and the nations turning to God. How does Jesus' suffering lead to hope?
"The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." What does it mean for the Lord to be your shepherd?
"He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul." Where do you need rest and restoring?
"Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me." What valley are you in?
"Goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life." How have you seen this?
"The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof." How does this change how you see the world?
"Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord? He who has clean hands and a pure heart." How does Jesus make this possible?
"Who is this King of glory?" How would you describe him?
"Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths." Where do you need God's teaching?
David asked God to remember his mercy, not his sins. What does this show about God?
"Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I am lonely and afflicted." Where do you need God's grace?
David walked in integrity and trusted the Lord. What does integrity look like for you?
"O Lord, I love the habitation of your house." What do you love about worshipping with God's people?
"The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?" What fear does this answer?
"One thing have I asked of the Lord... to gaze upon the beauty of the Lord." What is your "one thing"?
"Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage." What are you waiting for?
David cried for God not to be silent. When has God seemed silent to you?
"The Lord is my strength and my shield; in him my heart trusts, and I am helped." How has God helped you?
"Be their shepherd and carry them forever." Who would you ask God to carry?
"Ascribe to the Lord the glory due his name." What glory belongs to God?
The voice of the Lord is powerful, breaking cedars and shaking the wilderness. What does this show about God's word?
"May the Lord give strength to his people! May the Lord bless his people with peace!" Where do you need his strength and peace?
"You have drawn me up." From what has God lifted you?
"Weeping may tarry for the night, but joy comes with the morning." How does this give you hope?
"You have turned for me my mourning into dancing." When has God turned your sorrow into joy?
"Into your hand I commit my spirit." What do you need to commit into God's hands?
"My times are in your hand." How does this comfort you?
"Oh, how abundant is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who fear you." What goodness of God have you seen?
"Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven." What does forgiveness feel like?
David's body wasted away when he kept silent about his sin. Why does confession bring relief?
"I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go." Where do you need God's guidance?
"Sing to him a new song." What new reason do you have to praise God?
"By the word of the Lord the heavens were made." What does this show about the power of God's word?
"Our soul waits for the Lord; he is our help and our shield." How do you wait for God?
"I will bless the Lord at all times." What makes this hard?
"I sought the Lord, and he answered me and delivered me from all my fears." What fear do you need delivering from?
"Oh, taste and see that the Lord is good!" How have you tasted God's goodness?
"The Lord is near to the brokenhearted." Who do you know who is brokenhearted?
David asked God, "Say to my soul, 'I am your salvation!'" What do you need God to say to your soul?
David prayed for those who later turned against him. How do you respond to betrayal?
"Great is the Lord, who delights in the welfare of his servant!" What does it mean that God delights in your welfare?
"Your steadfast love, O Lord, extends to the heavens." How big is God's love to you?
"With you is the fountain of life; in your light do we see light." How does God give you life?
"Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart." How does delighting in God shape our desires?
"Commit your way to the Lord; trust in him... Be still before the Lord and wait patiently." What do you need to commit to him?
"The steps of a man are established by the Lord." How has God directed your steps?
David felt the weight of his sin. How does sin weigh us down?
"O Lord, all my longing is before you; my sighing is not hidden from you." What longings can you bring to God?
"Do not forsake me, O Lord... make haste to help me." Where do you need God's help?
"Let me know my end and what is the measure of my days." How does knowing life is short change your priorities?
"And now, O Lord, for what do I wait? My hope is in you." Where is your hope?
"I waited patiently for the Lord; he inclined to me and heard my cry. He drew me up from the pit." When has God lifted you?
"You have multiplied, O Lord my God, your wondrous deeds." Which of his deeds could you list?
"I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart." What does delighting in God's will look like?
"Blessed is the one who considers the poor!" How can you consider the poor?
Even a close friend lifted his heel against David. How does Jesus understand betrayal?
"Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting!" How can you bless the Lord today?
"As a deer pants for flowing streams, so pants my soul for you, O God." What does thirst for God look like?
"Why are you cast down, O my soul? Hope in God." How can you speak hope to your own soul?
"By day the Lord commands his steadfast love, and at night his song is with me." How is God with you day and night?
"Send out your light and your truth; let them lead me." Where do you need God's light?
"I will go to the altar of God, to God my exceeding joy." What makes God your joy?
"Not by their own sword did they win the land... but your right hand." What victories has God given you?
The people suffered though they had not forgotten God. How do you hold onto faith in unexplained suffering?
"Rise up; come to our help! Redeem us for the sake of your steadfast love!" What would you cry out for?
The king is "the most handsome of the sons of men; grace is poured upon your lips." How does this point to Jesus?
"Your throne, O God, is forever and ever." How does Hebrews use this of Jesus?
The bride is called to honour the king. What does it mean to belong to Christ?
"God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble." What trouble do you need his help in?
"The Lord of hosts is with us." What does God's presence mean to you?
"Be still, and know that I am God." How can you be still before God today?
"Clap your hands, all peoples! Shout to God with loud songs of joy!" What makes you joyful in God?
"God reigns over the nations." How does this give you hope for the world?
"Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised." What makes God great?
"We have thought on your steadfast love, O God." What do you think about when you think of God's love?
"This is God, our God forever and ever. He will guide us forever." How has God guided you?
No one can ransom another or give God the price of a life. How does Jesus pay the ransom?
"God will ransom my soul from the power of Sheol, for he will receive me." What hope does this give?
"When he dies he will carry nothing away." How does this shape your view of wealth?
"The Mighty One, God the Lord, speaks." How do you listen when God speaks?
"Every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills." What does this show about God's ownership?
"Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving... call upon me in the day of trouble." Which do you need to do?
"The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice glorifies me." What can you thank God for?
David prayed, "Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love." How does God's love meet your sin?
"Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me." What renewal do you need?
"Restore to me the joy of your salvation." Where have you lost joy?
"A broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise." What does a contrite heart look like?
David contrasts those who trust in riches and lies. What do you trust in?
"I am like a green olive tree in the house of God. I trust in the steadfast love of God forever." What makes you flourish?
"There is none who does good." What does this show about our need for grace?
"When God restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice." What restoration are you hoping for?
David cried for God to save him by his name. What does God's name mean to you?
"Behold, God is my helper." How has God helped you?
David promises a freewill offering. What would you freely offer God?
"Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and be at rest." When have you wanted to escape?
David was hurt by a close friend. How does God meet you in betrayal?
"Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you." What burden can you cast on him?
"When I am afraid, I put my trust in you." What fear do you need to bring to God?
"You have kept count of my tossings; put my tears in your bottle." What does it mean that God notices your tears?
God delivered David so he could walk before God in the light of life. How do you walk with God?
"In the shadow of your wings I will take refuge, till the storms of destruction pass by." What storm are you sheltering from?
"My heart is steadfast, O God! I will sing and make melody!" How can you praise God in trouble?
David speaks against unjust rulers. How does God view injustice?
"Surely there is a God who judges on earth." How does God's justice give hope?
"O my Strength, I will watch for you, for you, O God, are my fortress." What does it mean to watch for God?
"I will sing of your strength; I will sing aloud of your steadfast love in the morning." What can you sing of today?
The people felt God had rejected them. How do you pray when you feel far from God?
"Vain is the salvation of man! With God we shall do valiantly." Where do you need to trust God, not people?
"From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I." Where do you need that rock?
"Let me dwell in your tent forever!" What does it mean to dwell with God?
"For God alone my soul waits in silence; from him comes my salvation." How can you wait in silence for God?
"Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him." What do you need to pour out?
"If riches increase, set not your heart on them." Where is your heart set?
"My soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you, as in a dry and weary land." When have you felt this thirst?
"Your steadfast love is better than life." What does this mean to you?
David remembered God on his bed and clung to him. How can you remember God at night?
David asked God to hide him from the secret plots of the wicked. How do you handle being plotted against?
"Let the righteous one rejoice in the Lord and take refuge in him!" What makes you rejoice in God?
"Blessed is the one you choose and bring near." What does it mean to be brought near to God?
God is "the hope of all the ends of the earth." How does this shape your hope?
God crowns the year with his bounty. What good gifts has God crowned your year with?
"Shout for joy to God, all the earth." What can you praise God for?
"You have tried us as silver is tried... yet you have brought us out to a place of abundance." How has God refined you?
"Come and hear... and I will tell what he has done for my soul." What has God done for your soul?
"May God be gracious to us and bless us and make his face to shine upon us, that your way may be known on earth." How does God bless us for the sake of others?
"Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you!" How can you pray for the nations?
God is a father to the fatherless and settles the solitary in a home. How does God care for the lonely?
"Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears us up." How has God carried you today?
God gives power and strength to his people. Where do you need God's strength?
"Save me, O God! For the waters have come up to my neck." When have you felt overwhelmed?
"Zeal for your house has consumed me." How does this verse point to Jesus?
"In the abundance of your steadfast love answer me." How do you rely on God's love in prayer?
"I will praise the name of God with a song." How can you praise God even in trouble?
"Make haste, O God, to deliver me!" Where do you need God's quick help?
"I am poor and needy; hasten to me, O God!" What does it mean to come to God in need?
"You, O Lord, are my hope, my trust, O Lord, from my youth." How has God been with you through your life?
"I will hope continually and will praise you yet more and more." How can your praise grow?
"Even to old age... O God, do not forsake me, until I proclaim your might to another generation." Who could you pass faith on to?
The psalm prays for a king who defends the poor. How does Jesus fulfil this?
"He delivers the needy when he calls, the poor and him who has no helper." How can you help the needy?
"Blessed be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory!" How can you pray for God's glory to fill the earth?
Asaph envied the arrogant when he saw their prosperity. When are you tempted to envy?
"When I thought how to understand this... until I went into the sanctuary of God." How does worship change your perspective?
"Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire besides you." What does this mean to you?
"For me it is good to be near God." How can you draw near to God today?
"O God, why do you cast us off forever?" How can you bring hard questions to God?
"God my King is from of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth." How does remembering God's power help in hard times?
"We give thanks to you, O God... your name is near." How is God's name near to you?
"It is God who executes judgement, putting down one and lifting up another." How does this humble us?
"In Judah God is known." How is God known where you live?
God arose to save all the humble of the earth. What does this show about whom God cares for?
"Make your vows to the Lord your God and perform them." What have you promised God?
Asaph's soul refused to be comforted. When have you felt this way?
"Has his steadfast love forever ceased?" How do you answer this question?
"I will remember the deeds of the Lord." What deeds of God can you remember?
"Your way was through the sea... yet your footprints were unseen." How has God led you in ways you couldn't see?
"We will tell to the coming generation the glorious deeds of the Lord." How can you pass on God's story?
The aim was that children "should set their hope in God and not forget the works of God." How can you help children hope in God?
The people tested God and did not trust his saving power. Where do you doubt God's power?
"He, being compassionate, atoned for their iniquity... He remembered that they were but flesh." What does this show about God?
God chose David from the sheepfolds to shepherd his people with upright heart. How does this point to Jesus?
The psalmist grieved over Jerusalem's ruin. What grieves you about the state of the world?
"Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us, and atone for our sins." How does this prayer shape yours?
"We your people, the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever." What does it mean to be sheep of God's pasture?
"Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved!" Where do you need God's face to shine?
Israel is pictured as a vine God planted. What has God planted in your life?
"Let your hand be on the man of your right hand." How does this point to Jesus?
"Sing aloud to God our strength." How do you express joy in worship?
"Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it." What do you need God to fill?
"Oh, that my people would listen to me." What might God be saying that you need to listen to?
God calls rulers to defend the weak and the fatherless. How can you defend the vulnerable?
"Arise, O God, judge the earth." What injustice do you long for God to judge?
The nations plotted against God's people. How do you respond when you feel opposed?
"That they may know that you alone, whose name is the Lord, are the Most High over all the earth." How can God's name be known?
"How lovely is your dwelling place, O Lord of hosts!" What do you love about being with God?
"Blessed are those whose strength is in you... As they go through the Valley of Baca they make it a place of springs." How does God turn hard places into springs?
"A day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere." What does this mean to you?
"No good thing does he withhold from those who walk uprightly." How does this encourage you?
"You forgave the iniquity of your people." What does God's forgiveness mean to you?
"Will you not revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you?" Where do you need revival?
"Steadfast love and faithfulness meet; righteousness and peace kiss each other." How do these meet at the cross?
"You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in steadfast love to all who call upon you." What does this show about God?
"Teach me your way, O Lord, that I may walk in your truth; unite my heart to fear your name." Where is your heart divided?
"You, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious." How have you experienced his mercy?
"Glorious things of you are spoken, O city of God." What makes God's people glorious?
People from many nations are counted as born in Zion. What does this show about God's welcome?
The psalmist cried day and night, overwhelmed with troubles. How does it help that the Bible includes such dark prayers?
"Darkness is my closest friend." What would you say to someone who feels this way?
"I will sing of the steadfast love of the Lord, forever." What part of God's love would you sing about?
"Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne." What does this show about God's rule?
God promises David's throne will last forever. How is this fulfilled in Jesus?
"How long, O Lord?" How do you hold onto God's promises when they seem delayed?
"Lord, you have been our dwelling place in all generations." What does it mean that God is your home?
"Teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom." How does remembering life is short help you?
"Satisfy us in the morning with your steadfast love." What would it mean to be satisfied in God each morning?
"Establish the work of our hands." What work do you want God to establish?
"He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty." What does dwelling with God look like?
"He will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge." How does this picture comfort you?
"Because he holds fast to me in love, I will deliver him." What does God promise to those who love him?
"It is good to give thanks to the Lord... to declare your steadfast love in the morning, and your faithfulness by night." How can you do this today?
"The righteous flourish like the palm tree... They still bear fruit in old age." What does lifelong fruitfulness look like?
"The Lord reigns; he is robed in majesty." How does God's reign steady you?
"Mightier than the thunders of many waters... the Lord on high is mighty!" What "waters" feel overwhelming to you?
"Blessed is the man whom you discipline, O Lord." How has God taught you?
"When the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul." What cares do you need consoling in?
"The Lord has become my stronghold, and my God the rock of my refuge." Where do you need refuge?
"Let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation!" What can you praise God for?
"Come, let us worship and bow down... For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture." What does this mean to you?
"Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts." What is God saying to you today?
"Sing to the Lord a new song... declare his glory among the nations." How can you share God's glory?
"Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised." What makes God great to you?
All creation rejoices before the Lord, for he comes to judge in righteousness. Why is God's coming good news?
"The Lord reigns, let the earth rejoice." Why is God's reign a reason for joy?
"Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart." Where do you need light and joy?
"Oh sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done marvellous things!" What marvellous thing has God done for you?
"Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth." How can you join creation in praise?
"Holy is he!" What does God's holiness mean to you?
God answered Moses, Aaron and Samuel when they called. How does God answer you?
"Serve the Lord with gladness! Come into his presence with singing!" How can you serve God gladly?
"Know that the Lord, he is God! It is he who made us, and we are his." What does belonging to God mean?
"Enter his gates with thanksgiving... For the Lord is good; his steadfast love endures forever." What can you thank God for today?
David resolves to walk with integrity of heart within his house. What would integrity at home look like for you?
David wanted faithful people around him. Who are the faithful people in your life?
The psalmist was afflicted and felt like a lonely sparrow on a housetop. When have you felt this lonely?
"But you, O Lord, are enthroned forever." How does God's permanence help in hard times?
"They will perish, but you will remain... you are the same, and your years have no end." What comfort is this?
"Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits." Which benefits of God are you most thankful for?
"As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us." What does this mean for you?
"As a father shows compassion to his children, so the Lord shows compassion to those who fear him." How does this comfort you?
"The steadfast love of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting." How does God's lasting love compare with our short lives?
The psalmist pictures God clothed with light and riding on the clouds. What does this show about God's majesty?
God gives water to the animals and wine to gladden hearts. How do you see God's care in creation?
"O Lord, how manifold are your works! In wisdom have you made them all." What in creation amazes you?
"I will sing to the Lord as long as I live." What would you sing about today?
"Remember the wondrous works that he has done." What wondrous works of God can you remember?
"He remembers his covenant forever." How does God's faithfulness to his promises encourage you?
God sent Joseph ahead to save his family. How has God worked through hard things in your life?
"Oh give thanks to the Lord, for he is good." What goodness of God do you want to thank him for?
"They soon forgot his works." How quickly do you forget what God has done?
Many times God delivered them, and he remembered his covenant. What does this show about God's patience?
"Let the redeemed of the Lord say so." How would you tell your story of being redeemed?
"He satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good things." What are you longing for?
God stilled the storm and brought them to their desired haven. How has God calmed a storm for you?
"Whoever is wise, let him attend to these things; let them consider the steadfast love of the Lord." How can you consider God's love today?
"My heart is steadfast, O God! I will sing." How can your heart be steadfast?
"With God we shall do valiantly." Where do you need God's help to be brave?
David was repaid evil for good. How do you respond when your kindness is repaid with harm?
David prayed, "Deal on my behalf for your name's sake." What do you need God to do for you?
"He stands at the right hand of the needy one." How has God stood by you?
"The Lord says to my Lord: 'Sit at my right hand.'" How does Jesus use this verse to show who he is?
"You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek." How does Hebrews connect this to Jesus?
"Great are the works of the Lord, studied by all who delight in them." What work of God would you like to study?
"He sent redemption to his people." What does redemption mean to you?
"The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom." How does fearing God make you wise?
"Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, who greatly delights in his commandments!" What does delighting in God's commands look like?
The generous person "is not afraid of bad news; his heart is firm, trusting in the Lord." How does trust make us brave?
"From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is to be praised!" How can you praise God throughout your day?
"He raises the poor from the dust." What does this show about God's care for the lowly?
The sea fled and the mountains skipped when God brought Israel out of Egypt. What does this show about God's power?
God turns the rock into a pool of water. How has God provided in unexpected ways?
"Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory." Where are you tempted to take glory for yourself?
Idols have mouths but cannot speak. What idols do people trust today?
"Trust in the Lord! He is their help and their shield." How do you trust God more?
"I love the Lord, because he has heard my voice and my pleas for mercy." How has God heard you?
"Return, O my soul, to your rest; for the Lord has dealt bountifully with you." How has God dealt bountifully with you?
"What shall I render to the Lord for all his benefits to me?" How would you answer?
"Praise the Lord, all nations!" How does this short psalm show God's heart for the world?
"Great is his steadfast love toward us, and the faithfulness of the Lord endures forever." How has God's faithfulness lasted in your life?
"Oh give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!" What can you thank him for?
"It is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man." Where do you need to trust God rather than people?
"The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone." How does this point to Jesus?
"This is the day that the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it." What can you rejoice in today?
"Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the Lord!" What does walking in God's word look like?
"How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to your word." How does God's word keep you?
"I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you." Which verse could you store in your heart?
"Open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your law." Pray this before reading today.
"My soul clings to the dust; give me life according to your word!" Where do you need life from God's word?
"Incline my heart to your testimonies, and not to selfish gain!" What pulls your heart?
"This is my comfort in my affliction, that your promise gives me life." Which promise has comforted you?
"It is good for me that I was afflicted, that I might learn your statutes." What has hardship taught you?
"Forever, O Lord, your word is firmly fixed in the heavens." How does the permanence of God's word help you?
"Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation all the day." How can God's word be your meditation?
"Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path." Where do you need God's light?
"The unfolding of your words gives light." How has God's word given you understanding?
"I rise before dawn and cry for help; I hope in your words." How can you start your day with God's word?
"Great peace have those who love your law." What peace has God's word given you?
"I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant." Where do you need the Shepherd to seek you?
"In my distress I called to the Lord, and he answered me." When has God answered you in distress?
"I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war." How can you pursue peace?
"I lift up my eyes to the hills. From where does my help come? My help comes from the Lord." Where do you look for help?
"He who keeps you will not slumber." What does it mean that God never sleeps?
"The Lord will keep your going out and your coming in." How does God keep you day by day?
"I was glad when they said to me, 'Let us go to the house of the Lord!'" What makes you glad about worshipping together?
"Pray for the peace of Jerusalem." How can you pray for the peace of God's people?
"As the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, so our eyes look to the Lord." What does it mean to keep your eyes on God?
"Have mercy upon us, O Lord." Where do you need God's mercy?
"If it had not been the Lord who was on our side..." When has God been on your side?
"Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth." How does this help you?
"As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the Lord surrounds his people." How does God surround you?
"Do good, O Lord, to those who are good, and to those who are upright in their hearts." Who could you pray this for?
"The Lord has done great things for us; we are glad." What great things has God done for you?
"Those who sow in tears shall reap with shouts of joy!" Where are you sowing in tears?
"Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labour in vain." What are you building, and is God in it?
"He gives to his beloved sleep." How can you rest in God instead of anxious toil?
"Children are a heritage from the Lord." How can you bless the children around you?
"Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways!" What does walking in God's ways look like at home?
"May you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life!" How can you pray for God's people?
"Greatly have they afflicted me... yet they have not prevailed against me." How has God sustained you?
"The Lord is righteous; he has cut the cords of the wicked." What has God set you free from?
"If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, who could stand? But with you there is forgiveness." What does this mean to you?
"My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning." What are you waiting for?
"With the Lord there is steadfast love, and with him is plentiful redemption." How have you seen this?
"I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother." How can you quiet your soul before God?
"Hope in the Lord from this time forth and forevermore." Where do you need hope?
David would not rest until he found a place for the Lord. What priority do you give to God?
God swore to David a sure oath. How does God's oath point to Jesus?
God chose Zion as his dwelling place. What does it mean that God chooses to dwell with his people?
"How good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell in unity!" How can you help your fellowship be united?
Unity is like precious oil and refreshing dew. What does unity bring to a community?
"Lift up your hands to the holy place and bless the Lord!" How can you bless the Lord at the end of your day?
"May the Lord bless you from Zion." Who could you bless today?
"Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good." What goodness of God moves you to praise?
"Whatever the Lord pleases, he does." How does God's sovereignty comfort you?
Idols have eyes but cannot see. What false securities do people rely on?
"Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever." What would you add to this psalm from your own life?
"It is he who remembered us in our low estate." When has God remembered you in a low place?
"How shall we sing the Lord's song in a foreign land?" When has praise felt hard?
The exiles vowed never to forget Jerusalem. What do you never want to forget about God?
"On the day I called, you answered me; my strength of soul you increased." How has God strengthened you?
"Though the Lord is high, he regards the lowly." What does this show about God?
"The Lord will fulfil his purpose for me." What purpose do you trust God to fulfil?
"O Lord, you have searched me and known me!" How does it feel to be fully known by God?
"Where shall I go from your Spirit?" How does God's presence everywhere comfort you?
"I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made." How does this change how you see yourself?
"Search me, O God, and know my heart!" What do you want God to search in you?
David prayed for protection from violent people. How do you pray when you feel unsafe?
"The Lord will maintain the cause of the afflicted." How does God care for the afflicted?
"Let my prayer be counted as incense before you." What does it mean for prayer to be like incense?
"Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth." What words do you need God to guard?
"No one cares for my soul." When have you felt this way?
"You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living." What does it mean for God to be your portion?
"I remember the days of old... I stretch out my hands to you." How does remembering God help you pray?
"Let me hear in the morning of your steadfast love, for in you I trust." How can you start each day with God's love?
"Teach me to do your will, for you are my God!" What does doing God's will look like today?
"What is man that you regard him?" How does it feel that God regards you?
"Blessed are the people whose God is the Lord!" What blessings come from belonging to God?
"Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised, and his greatness is unsearchable." What about God's greatness amazes you?
"The Lord is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love." How have you seen this?
"The Lord upholds all who are falling and raises up all who are bowed down." Where do you need God to raise you?
"The Lord is near to all who call on him." How can you call on him today?
"Put not your trust in princes." Where are you tempted to put your trust?
"Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob." How does God help the oppressed, the hungry and the prisoner?
"He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds." Where do you need God's healing?
"He determines the number of the stars; he gives to all of them their names." What does this show about God's care?
"The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his steadfast love." What does God take pleasure in?
The heavens and angels praise the Lord. How does all creation point to God?
All the earth, from sea creatures to kings, is called to praise. How can you join creation's praise?
"The Lord takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation." How does it feel that God delights in you?
"Let the godly exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds." How can you praise God at rest?
"Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his excellent greatness!" What mighty deed of God would you praise?
The psalm calls for every instrument to praise God. How do you like to praise him?
"Let everything that has breath praise the Lord!" How can your whole life be praise today?
